questions.q: What does the "CUDA Version" field in nvidia-smi's output actually represent?
options: The exact CUDA Toolkit version installed on the system
The maximum CUDA version the installed driver supports
The version of PyTorch currently installed
The version of nvcc currently running
questions.explain: The CUDA Version shown in nvidia-smi is a ceiling — the maximum CUDA version the installed driver can support — not necessarily the version of anything actually installed.

options: The NVIDIA driver version installed on the system
The CUDA runtime version that specific PyTorch build was compiled against
The maximum CUDA version supported by the GPU hardware
The version of nvidia-smi installed
questions.explain: torch.version.cuda reports the CUDA runtime version that particular PyTorch build was compiled against, which is independent of whatever CUDA Toolkit (if any) is installed on the system.

questions.q: Why can PyTorch run GPU workloads on a machine without the full CUDA Toolkit installed?
options: PyTorch does not actually use CUDA
Modern PyTorch wheels bundle their own copy of the CUDA runtime libraries
The NVIDIA driver substitutes for the Toolkit automatically
PyTorch always falls back to CPU execution
questions.explain: Modern PyTorch wheels ship their own bundled CUDA runtime libraries, so a full CUDA Toolkit installation (with nvcc, headers, etc.) is often unnecessary just to run PyTorch on a GPU.

questions.q: If a driver reports a maximum supported CUDA version of 12.4, can it run software built against CUDA 11.8?
options: No, the versions must match exactly
Yes, because CUDA compatibility runs backward — a newer driver can run software built against an older CUDA version
Only if the Toolkit is uninstalled first
Only on data-center GPUs, never on consumer GPUs
questions.explain: CUDA version compatibility runs backward: a driver supporting up to CUDA 12.4 can run software built against CUDA 12.0, 11.8, or earlier versions.

questions.q: When does a CUDA version mismatch actually cause a real problem?
options: Whenever nvcc --version and torch.version.cuda report different numbers
When the installed driver's maximum supported CUDA version is lower than what PyTorch requires
Whenever more than one CUDA Toolkit version is installed on the same machine
Only when running on a laptop GPU instead of a data-center GPU
questions.explain: Mismatches between nvcc, torch.version.cuda, and nvidia-smi's reported max version are usually harmless. The real problem case is when the installed driver's maximum supported version is lower than what the PyTorch build requires, which can cause torch.cuda.is_available() to return False or kernel launches to fail.
